meta.title: Check on Claude Code or Codex from your phone
meta.description: Run coding agents in tmux and open that pane from a phone anywhere — read the diff, answer the approval prompt, start the next task. No SSH key, no VPN.

hero.title: Long agent runs, checked from wherever you are.
hero.lead: Agentic runs are long, chatty and easy to abandon. Run them in tmux — as most people already do — and mtmux gives you the same pane on a phone, so walking away stops meaning losing the thread.
hero.note: mtmux <post>does not notify you</post>. There is no push, no watcher and no agent detection. It is the session, on your phone, in about two seconds.

workflow.title: What the loop actually looks like
workflow.description: Nothing here is mtmux-specific except step three. The agent runs in a normal tmux session the whole time.

steps.title: Start the run in tmux
steps.body: <cmd>tmux new -s work</cmd>, then start Claude Code, Codex, aider or whatever you use. It is <post>an ordinary tmux session</post> — mtmux never wraps or supervises the process.

steps.title: Leave the desk
steps.body: The tmux server keeps the pty alive exactly as it always has. Closing the laptop lid does not touch it.

steps.title: Open the session on your phone
steps.body: Scan the code once, and after that the browser is trusted. Reopening the tab reattaches to the live pane.

steps.title: Read, answer, or start the next one
steps.body: The modifier row gives you a real esc, ctrl and prefix key, so a y/n approval is one tap and a new task is a normal command.

does.title: What mtmux does
items: Serves the tmux session your agent is already running in, unmodified.
Shows the pane's real output, byte for byte, with scrollback and search.
Sends your keystrokes to that pane, including approval answers and interrupts.
Keeps working over cellular, and reattaches on its own after a dropout.
Encrypts everything end to end, so the relay carries ciphertext it cannot read.

doesNot.title: What it does not do
items: It does not notify you. No push, no email, no Slack, no webhook.
It does not detect agents, parse panes or match on output signatures.
It does not know the difference between finished, blocked and stalled.
It does not wrap your command or watch an exit code.
It will not wake you at 3am, because it cannot wake you at all.

scope.note: If being paged is what you need, that is a real requirement and mtmux is not it — <post>a tmux hook</post> piping into <cmd>ntfy</cmd>, or your agent's own hook support, will serve you better. mtmux solves the other half: once you know you want to look, looking is trivial.

timeline.title: A morning with three agents running

items.text: Kicked off a refactor in <path>work:1</path> and walked to the train.
Opened the tab on the platform. Codex was sitting on <accent>Apply patch?</accent> in <path>api:0</path> — tapped <accent>y</accent>.
Looked again at <path>web:2</path>: no new output for a while. Scrolled up, found a hung installer, killed it and restarted.
Refactor finished, 27 tests green. Read the diff on the phone and queued the follow-up task.
Sat down at the desk. Same three sessions, exactly where the phone left them.

timeline.note: Every check in that morning was something you chose to do. Nothing buzzed.

faq.title: Questions about running agents this way

items.question: Does mtmux notify me when Claude Code finishes?
items.answer: No. mtmux has no notification system at all — no push, no email, no Slack. It gives you a session you can open from a phone in a couple of seconds and read. If you want <post>Claude Code itself to page you</post>, wire that up separately; the two are complementary, not alternatives.

items.question: Does it work with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI or aider?
items.answer: With all of them, and with anything else that runs in a terminal, because mtmux does not know or care what is in the pane. It attaches to tmux. If your tool runs in tmux today, it works today, with no preset and no configuration. <post>Being paged when Codex CLI stops</post> is a separate job for a separate tool — mtmux only shows you the pane.

items.question: Can I answer an approval prompt from my phone?
items.answer: Yes — it is a normal keystroke to a normal pane. The on-screen modifier row keeps esc, ctrl, alt, tab and the arrows reachable, so y, n, ctrl-c and your prefix key are all one tap.

items.question: Do I have to change how I start my agent?
items.answer: No. Start it however you already do, inside a tmux session. mtmux never wraps the process, never injects a shim and never reads its exit code — it is a client attaching to the tmux server, the same as tmux attach.

items.question: What if the agent is producing enormous amounts of output?
items.answer: The pane renders as it does anywhere else, and scrollback and search work, so you can jump to the part you care about. A pane redrawing a full screen continuously is the expensive case for any browser terminal, including this one.

items.question: Is my code going through your servers?
items.answer: Encrypted, and only if you use the tunnel. The relay forwards frames sealed with keys derived on your machine and in your browser, so it carries ciphertext it cannot read. On your own network, mtmux start --local never contacts us at all.

cta.title: Your agent is still running. Go look at it.
cta.description: One command on the machine, one scan on the phone. No account, and nothing to configure per agent.
